name: Pekka Laurila
profile: Finnish engineer who met Rafal Modrzewski at Aalto University, where they set out to monitor Arctic sea ice from space and co-founded ICEYE. Now Chief Strategy Officer, he helped build the company into an operator of a constellation of small synthetic-aperture-radar satellites (now on its fifth satellite generation), serving defense, insurance and government customers; valued ~$3B.
interesting_fact: The industry said a radar satellite under 100 kg was impossible; in 2018 ICEYE-X1 became the first SAR satellite under 100 kg and Finland's first commercial satellite.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he shared the Finnish Engineering Award with Modrzewski, Antti Kestila and Aalto's Jaan Praks and Tuomas Tikka for creating Finland's space-technology sector, which grew from student course work on the 'milk bottle-sized' Aalto-1 nanosatellite.
notes: Named, with Modrzewski, an EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year 2026 finalist (Finland). Press inquiries go through ICEYE's press form.

name: Noah Tweedale
profile: English entrepreneur in his twenties who co-founded Pump.fun with Alon Cohen and Dylan Kerler; the platform launched in January 2024 and lets anyone create and trade memecoins, taking a 1% cut of trades. It reportedly earned over $350M in revenue in its first year, and its July 2025 PUMP token sale raised about $1.3B.
interesting_fact: The three founders started out as memecoin traders themselves and built Pump.fun after repeatedly being hit by rug pulls; Tweedale told WIRED the idea was 'to build something where everyone was on the same playing field.'
deep_cut_fact: He goes by the online pseudonym 'Sapijiju'; the founders met in England and kept their identities secret until corporate filings surfaced their names.
notes: Very privacy- and security-conscious; agreed to WIRED interview only on condition his whereabouts/appearance stayed undisclosed. Platform faces regulatory and legal scrutiny (UK FCA warning, US lawsuit) - handle carefully. No press email found.

name: Mark Groden
current_role: Founder & CEO, Skyryse (aviation automation, El Segundo, CA)
profile: Engineer with a PhD in sensor data fusion who founded Skyryse in 2016 to make flying simpler and safer. Its SkyOS flight-automation system and Skyryse One helicopter replace traditional controls with a software-defined, single-stick interface; the company works with private operators and the U.S. military and was valued at ~$1.15B in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: On 22 July 2023 SkyOS executed what the company called the world's first fully automated autorotation emergency landing, in a modified Robinson R66 helicopter.
deep_cut_fact: He holds more than 60 patents in aerial-vehicle automation, and his drive came from learning to fly as a teenager, when he saw first-hand how overwhelmed pilots can become.
notes: Skyryse hired ex-FAA head Michael Huerta and ex-NTSB chair Chris Hart as certification advisors (2021).

name: Efe Cakarel
current_role: Founder & CEO, MUBI (curated film streaming, distribution and production)
profile: Turkish-born entrepreneur (MIT EECS, Stanford MBA, ex-Goldman Sachs banker) who founded MUBI, which grew from a curated arthouse streaming service into a distributor and producer. MUBI had a hit with The Substance, made the biggest Cannes 2025 acquisition (Die My Love, $24M) and raised $100M from Sequoia at a $1B valuation in 2025.
interesting_fact: The New York Times profiled MUBI in February 2025 as 'a real Hollywood player' after the success of The Substance.
deep_cut_fact: He was on Turkey's national math team and placed third in the European Math Olympiad; he also holds two patents on monetizing web applications.
notes: Attended the American Collegiate Institute in Izmir. Avoid the 2025 Sequoia-investment controversy in outreach.
